section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: This subtitle establishes:

para.text: Procedures for designating a hospital as a trauma or specialty referral center;
Standards for a designated center to provide trauma or specialty care service;
Procedures for corrective action to be taken if a trauma or specialty referral center fails to comply with this subtitle; and
Procedures for the collection and use of trauma or specialty care data by MIEMSS to monitor and evaluate the trauma and specialty care systems.
In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Adult burn center” means:
An in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive burn treatment services to burn patients 15 years old or older; or

An out-of-State hospital that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS and that has been approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive burn treatment services to burn patients 15 years old or older.
“Adult trauma center” means:
An in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive trauma services to trauma patients 15 years old and older; or

An out-of-State hospital that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS and that has been approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive trauma treatment services to trauma patients 15 years old and older.
“Advanced Burn Life Support (ABLS®)” means a course developed and approved by the American Burn Association.
“Advanced Pediatric Life Support (APLS®)” means a course developed and approved by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP).
“Advanced practice professionals (APPs)” are licensed and credentialed nurse practitioners (NPs), nurse anesthetists, midwives, clinical nurse specialists (CNS) and physician assistants (PAs).
“Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS®)” means a course developed and approved by the American College of Surgeons.

“Appropriately trained” means a health care provider who has received the necessary training to develop the knowledge and skills needed for the appropriate care of the trauma or specialty care patient.
“Approved” means a formal process of review and acceptance by the appropriate authority.
“Attending” means a physician who has completed the formal training for the physician’s specialty and whose practice privileges are delineated by the hospital’s medical staff.
“Attending burn staff surgeon” means a surgeon appointed by the adult or pediatric burn center director with credentials and privileges appropriate to the burn service.
“Board certified” means a physician certified by an appropriate specialty board recognized by the American Board of Medical Specialties.

“Board eligible” means a physician qualified to take the examination to complete the certification process as specified by an appropriate specialty board that is recognized by the American Board of Medical Specialties.
“Burn care director” means a surgeon designated by the institution and medical staff to coordinate the activities of the adult or pediatric burn center.

“Burn care system” means a coordinated component of an emergency medical services system which encompasses one or more adult or pediatric burn centers and features communication links to, and triage-transfer protocols between, health care facilities, prehospital personnel, and transportation services.
“Burn Center” means an adult or pediatric burn center in Maryland unless otherwise indicated.
“Burn service” means a clinical service established by the medical staff which has responsibility for burn patients.
“Burn team” means a group of health care professionals organized to provide care to the burn patient in a coordinated system of care.
“Burn unit” means a specific area within the adult or pediatric burn center that:
Has committed the resources necessary to meet the criteria for an adult or pediatric burn center; and
Contains beds and other physical equipment related to care of the patient with burn injury.

“Bypass” means the temporary diversionary status of a trauma or specialty referral center that is requested and identified in the Emergency Department Advisory System (EDAS) due to a lack of staff, facilities, or equipment.

“Continuing education (CE)” means education provided for adults after they have left the formal education system consisting of short or part-time courses that brings participants up to date in a particular area of knowledge or skills.
“Continuing medical education (CME)” means training approved for credit by an entity accredited by the Accreditation Council of Continuing Medical Education.
“Credentialing” means a hospital's process for granting practice privileges to health care clinicians.
“Data quality guideline” means a written procedure for ascertaining the accuracy and completeness of data.
“Dedicated” means a designated resource that is exclusively for a specific trauma or specialty care program.
“Definitive care” means a level of therapeutic intervention capable of providing comprehensive services for a patient's particular injuries, or associated conditions, or both.
“Designation” means a process by which a hospital is identified by MIEMSS as an appropriate facility to receive patients with particular injuries or illnesses.
“Desirable” means a component of the standards that is encouraged but not required for designation.
“Emergency department (ED)” means a department or patient care area within a hospital that:
Is sufficiently staffed, equipped, and organized to provide emergency medical care at all times;
Is available to the public at all times; and
Is staffed by at least one qualified physician at all times.
Emergency Medical Services.
“Emergency medical services (EMS)” means a comprehensive system of emergency medical care that starts with prevention and continues through rehabilitation.
“Emergency medical services (EMS)” includes:
Comprehensive EMS, trauma, and specialty care system legislation, regulations, and policies;
Medical oversight and physician involvement;
Trained volunteer, career, and commercial personnel;
State and local government resource management and administration;
Integrated communications system including 911 centers, medical consultation centers, ambulances, and receiving hospitals;
Medical ground, air, and water transportation systems;
Cooperating facilities including hospitals, trauma centers, and specialty referral centers;
Public information, education, and prevention programs; and
Data collection, evaluation, quality improvement, and research.
“EMS clinician” means an individual certified or licensed by a state to provide out-of-hospital emergency medical services.
“EMS plan” means the plan to ensure effective coordination and evaluation of emergency medical services delivered in the State, as developed and approved by the EMS Board.

“Emergent consultation” means a physician consultation required for evaluation of known or potentially unstable condition, conditions requiring time sensitive interventions, or other reasons as determined and documented by the attending physician, surgeon, or emergency physician.
“Essential” means a component of the standards that is required for designation.
“Executive Director” means the Executive Director of MIEMSS.
Repealed.
“Fellowship” means formal, advanced, post-residency, specialty training.
Repealed.
“Geographic service area” means the area defined by the EMS Board that is normally served by a designated hospital for patients with a particular illness or injury.
“Immediately available” means a source available as soon as it is requested.
“Immediate response” means reacting at once to a patient care need.
“In-house” means physically present in the hospital.
“Injury surveillance” means routine monitoring of the type of injury and incidence for a specific population.
“Inpatient discharge data” means certain information from inpatient hospital records that is submitted by the hospital to the Health Services Cost Review Commission as required by law.
“Interfacility transfer” means the transfer of a patient from one hospital to another hospital.
“Learning outcomes” means an individual's performance, which can be measured by objective means, that results from the individual's participation in an educational program.
“Level I trauma center” means a hospital that:
Meets the Level I trauma center standards in COMAR 30.08.05; and
Is designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board.
“Level II trauma center” means a hospital that:
Meets the Level II trauma center standards in COMAR 30.08.05; and
Is designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board.
Repealed.
“Level III perinatal referral center” means a hospital that:
Meets the Level III perinatal referral center standards in COMAR 30.08.12;
Is designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board as capable of providing medical intensive care to newborns of all:
Gestational ages; and
Birth weights.
“Level III trauma center” means a community hospital with a trauma program that:
Meets the Level III trauma center standards in COMAR 30.08.05; and
Is designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board.
“Level IV perinatal referral center” means a hospital that:
Meets the Level IV perinatal referral center standards in COMAR 30.08.12; and
Is designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board as capable of providing comprehensive neonatal and obstetrical services, including all subspecialty services.

“Maryland Trauma Registry Data Dictionary for Adult Patients” means the listing of data inclusion criteria, data elements and audit filters to be collected for patients with traumatic injuries treated in a Maryland Trauma Center which is incorporated by reference in COMAR 30.01.02.01(B)(2).
“Maternal-fetal medicine” means a subspecialty recognized by the American Board of Obstetrics and Gynecology which addresses the medical care of high-risk pregnant women and their fetuses.
Most Critical Patients.
“Most critical patients” means those patients who:
Have confirmed BP< 90 mmHg at any time in adults and age-specific hypotension;
Have a gunshot wound to the head, neck, chest, or abdomen attributed to trauma;
Have a Glasgow Coma Score <9 with mechanism attributed to trauma;
Are transferred from other hospitals while receiving blood or vasoactive medication to maintain vital signs;
Are intubated and transferred from the scene; or
Have a respiratory compromise or are in need of an emergent airway, including intubated patients who are transferred from another facility.
“Most critical patients” includes those patients who:
Have a tourniquet or pelvic binder applied;
Are currently in Cardiac arrest or receiving CPR;
Have presence of motor paralysis;
Have an amputation proximal to the ankle or wrist;
Have Hypoxia as evidenced by pulse oximetry <90 percent;
Have uncontrolled external hemorrhage; or
Penetrating torso injury with evisceration.

“Multidisciplinary committee” means a group of health care professionals from two or more professional disciplines within a trauma or specialty referral center that reflects the multidisciplinary nature of trauma or specialty care.
“Multiple casualty incident (MCI)” means two or more injured people requiring emergency care simultaneously.

“National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB)” means the American College of Surgeons (ACS) aggregated trauma registry of [standardization of key trauma] standardized key data elements for research and improving care for trauma patients.

“Neonatal referral center” means an out-of-State facility that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS which has been approved by the EMS Board to accept transfers in order to provide neonatal care.
“Neonate” means a patient who is less than 28 days old.
“Neonatologist” means a pediatrician certified in neonatology by the American Board of Pediatrics.
“Neurotrauma center” means an in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide specialized care of traumatic brain injured and spinal cord injured patients.
“Nurse manager” means a registered nurse who has a full-time commitment to a specific patient care unit and is administratively responsible for the nursing service of that unit.
“Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH)” means the unit within Maryland's Executive Branch responsible for scheduling and conducting administrative hearings.
“Office of Care Integration” means the office within MIEMSS that is responsible for the verification and reverification of trauma and specialty care referral centers.
“On call” means committed for a specific time period to be available and respond within a specific amount of time to provide care for a patient in the hospital.
On-Site Review Record.
“On-site review record” means any record of the on-site visit and of the on-site review team.
“On-site review record” includes, but is not limited to:
Proceedings;
Records;
Files;
Notes;
Deliberations;
Reports;
Documents;
Statements;
Minutes; and
Any other oral or written communication.
“Optional” means a component of the standards that may be present or available but is not required for designation.
“Outcome” means a measurable health status that follows as a result of an injury or illness.
“Patient care log” means a list of patients' names and other information that is recorded by hospitals or emergency medical services agencies.
“Patient care record” means a record that contains information regarding the assessment and the care provided to a patient by any health care clinician in any practice setting.
“Patient discharge summary” means an abbreviated narrative, created after discharge from a health care facility, of a patient's record during that hospitalization.
“Patient identifier” means a unique number that is assigned to only one patient in order to identify records pertaining to the evaluation and care of that particular patient.
“Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS®)” means a pediatric resuscitation course developed and approved by the American Heart Association.
“Pediatric burn center” means:
An in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive burn treatment services to burn patients that have not reached their fifteenth (15th) birthday; or

An out-of-State hospital that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS and that has been approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive burn treatment services to burn patients who have not reached their fifteenth (15th) birthday.
“Pediatric trauma center” means:
An in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive trauma services to trauma patients who have not reached their fifteenth (15th) birthday; or

An out-of-State hospital that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS and that has been approved by the EMS Board to provide compressive trauma treatment services to trauma patients who have not reached their fifteenth (15th) birthday.
“Perinatal referral center” means:
An in-State hospital designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive obstetrical and neonatal services; or
An out-of-State hospital that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS that has been approved by the EMS Board to provide comprehensive obstetrical and neonatal services.
Repealed.
“Physical plant” means a building and associated structures.
“Postgraduate year (PGY)” means a classification system for residents indicating the year of post-medical school residency.
“Prehospital service” means a service that is provided from the time of injury or illness until the patient arrives in the hospital.

“Preliminary investigation” means fact finding and information gathering to enable MIEMSS to determine whether justification exists to initiate corrective action or to conduct a further investigation.

“Primary Adult Resource Center (PARC)” means a comprehensive trauma center, including a dedicated trauma care facility, dedicated staff and services, and designated, specialized, advanced training and research programs, which meets the PARC standards in COMAR 30.08.05 and which, in Maryland, is defined in statute as the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center.
“Promptly available” means a resource available within 30 minutes of the time it was requested.
“Protocol” means a written procedure to ensure standardization of a process.
“Quality management (QM)” means the quality management of trauma and specialty care services.
“Quality management program record” means a documented record related to quality management activities.
“Readily available” means a resource available for use a short time after it is requested.
“Resuscitation” means the phase of trauma or specialty care where emergency life support treatment is provided to sustain vital body functions.
“Reverification” means the process by which MIEMSS renews a trauma or specialty referral center's designation status.
“Sonologist” means a physician with special training in ultrasonography.
“Specialty referral center” means:
An in-State hospital that has been designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide care for a specific patient population with special care needs; or
An out-of-State facility that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS which has been approved by the EMS Board to provide specialty care.
“State Trauma Registry” means a database of information, submitted to MIEMSS by hospitals, relating to the care of trauma and burn patients that is used to evaluate the quality of care provided.

“SYSCOM/EMRC” means the Systems Communications/Emergency Medical Resource Center, an EMS communications center located within MIEMSS, that is used for coordination of medical communication on a Statewide basis.
“Transfer agreement” means a formal agreement between hospitals for the acceptance and transfer of patients.
“Transporting service” means an agency or entity providing patient care transport.
“Transport vehicle” means a vehicle or other conveyance used to transport patients.
“Trauma” means a major single system or multisystem injury or mechanism of injury which results in a possibility of disability or death.
Trauma Center.
“Trauma center” means a hospital that has been designated by MIEMSS and approved by the EMS Board to provide care to trauma patients.
“Trauma center” includes an out-of-State facility that has entered into an agreement with MIEMSS and has been approved by the EMS Board to provide care to trauma patients.
“Trauma Network (TraumaNet)” means an organization of representatives of trauma centers which includes trauma surgeons, trauma coordinators, and hospital administrators.
“Trauma panel” means the group of physicians within a specific trauma center credentialed by the trauma center hospital to provide trauma care.
“Trauma patient care resource” means the physical facilities, equipment, supplies, and medical personnel that are:
Used to provide care to trauma patients; and
Identified as immediately available, readily available, or promptly available.

“Trauma Quality Improvement Committee (TQIC)” is a medical review committee established by MIEMSS as an advisory body for quality issues and evaluation affecting the care of trauma patients and the Maryland Trauma System. The TQIC addresses issues primarily related to the system-wide delivery of trauma care across the continuum (pre-hospital care to discharge from the trauma center) identifying performance improvement activities and indicators to support resolution strategies.
“Trauma resuscitation team” means a group of trauma trained health care clinicians at the patient’s bedside following trauma team activation.

“Trauma service” means a group of trauma-trained physicians who are responsible for the initial resuscitation and care of trauma patients, including trauma/general surgery, emergency medicine, neurosurgery, and orthopedic surgery.
“Trend” means a tendency toward a particular conclusion or end point, usually determined by an analysis of data.

“Triage” means the sorting of patients in terms of priority, treatment, transportation, and destination, so that the patient can be transported to an appropriate hospital according to triage protocols.
“Unit of care” means the hospital subunit where the patient is receiving care at any point in time.

“Verification” means the process by which MIEMSS determines that a hospital that is applying for a particular designation status is in substantial compliance with the standards for the designation requested.
Under Education Article, §13-504, Annotated Code of Maryland, MIEMSS is the State administrative agency responsible for the coordination of all emergency medical services.
MIEMSS shall:
With the approval of the EMS Board, verify and designate hospitals to be trauma or specialty referral centers;
Establish standards for trauma and specialty care, triage, and transfer protocols for injured patients;
Establish and manage the State Trauma Registry;
Facilitate the establishment of Statewide, inclusive, trauma and specialty care systems by encouraging all hospitals to participate in:
The Statewide data collection process, and
Prevention programs;
Develop a quality management and improvement program to:
Monitor compliance with this subtitle by hospitals in the Statewide trauma and specialty care systems, and
Identify areas for enhancement;
With the consultation and advice of appropriate persons, develop and periodically review:
Prehospital trauma and specialty referral center triage criteria guidelines,
Interfacility transfer criteria for adult and pediatric patients,
Trauma and specialty referral center standards, and
Trauma registry and specialty referral center data;

Periodically evaluate the effectiveness of the Statewide trauma and specialty care systems and its component subsystems by using trauma registry and other appropriate data to identify and analyze system and patient care trends and outcomes;
Periodically conduct special studies of the Statewide trauma and specialty care systems to evaluate:
System access,
Capacity,
Quality,
Patient care outcomes, and
The financial condition of the system components;
Consult with appropriate persons in determining the need for trauma or specialty care services;
Facilitate and, where necessary, develop and maintain, public information, education, and prevention programs as an integral component of the trauma and specialty care systems;
As necessary, recommend to the EMS Board additional regulations to ensure the quality of the Statewide trauma and specialty care systems;
Provide technical assistance and support to hospitals and clinicians as necessary to implement the components of the EMS Plan; and
As necessary, verify compliance with trauma and specialty care standards by:

Reviewing, inspecting, evaluating, and auditing trauma and specialty care patient records, trauma and specialty care quality improvement committee minutes, and any other documents relevant to trauma and specialty care in any trauma or specialty referral center, and
Inspecting a trauma or specialty center's physical plant.

With the approval of the EMS Board, MIEMSS may enter into agreements with out-of-State trauma and specialty center hospitals where necessary to ensure access of patients to appropriate levels of trauma and specialty care. Such agreements are tantamount to designation by MIEMSS and approval by the EMS Board.

section.heading: Trauma Care Levels and Specialty Referral Centers.

para.text: MIEMSS shall designate a hospital by level of care capability as set forth for:
Trauma centers, in COMAR 30.08.05; or
Specialty referral centers, in the appropriate specialty care standards within this subtitle.
The levels of trauma care are:
Primary Adult Resource Center;
Level I trauma center;
Level II trauma center; or
Level III trauma center.
Multiple Clinical Locations.
A single hospital or one or more hospitals under common ownership may be designated as a single trauma or specialty referral center with more than one clinical location if:
Clinical requirements are met at each separate location;
There is a designated individual with administrative oversight of the designated trauma or specialty referral center;
There is a designated individual with clinical oversight of the designated trauma or specialty referral center who is responsible for:
Data collection;
Quality improvement;
Education;
Research; and
Prevention;
There is a designated individual responsible for administrative oversight at each clinical location; and
There is a designated individual responsible for clinical oversight at each clinical location.
In this subtitle, in the case of a designated trauma or specialty center with more than one clinical location:

The term “hospital” shall be interpreted as meaning each separate clinical location which is operated as part of the designated trauma or specialty center program for the purposes of clinical requirements; and

The term “hospital” shall be interpreted to mean all clinical locations operated as part of the designated trauma or specialty center program collectively for the purposes of nonclinical requirements.
The EMS Board shall:
Determine the number and level of trauma and specialty referral centers to be designated; and

For specialty referral centers that require a certificate of need from the Maryland Health Care Commission, establish the criteria for the number of specialty referral centers in coordination with the Maryland Health Care Commission.
The EMS Board shall consider:
Access to trauma or specialty care;
Level of care;
Capacity to provide the care; and
Timeliness of care received.
MIEMSS may consult with appropriate State agencies in determining the need for trauma or specialty services for a hospital's geographic service area.
To be eligible for consideration by MIEMSS as a designated trauma or specialty referral center, a hospital shall meet the standards set forth for such a center in this subtitle.

MIEMSS shall solicit applications for trauma and specialty referral center designation from any interested hospital, including all current trauma and specialty referral centers, by publication of the solicitation in the Maryland Register.
MIEMSS may periodically solicit applications for trauma and specialty referral center designation, as needed, by publication of the solicitation in the Maryland Register.
Hospitals may seek verification for designation as a trauma or specialty referral center irrespective of solicitation of interest by MIEMSS by notifying the MIEMSS Office of Care Integration.
MIEMSS shall provide the applicant with appropriate application materials in paper or electronic form for trauma or specialty referral center designation.

An applicant for trauma or specialty referral center designation shall submit an application to the Office of Care Integration in a form specified by MIEMSS, which shall include, but not be limited to, submitting evidence of the applicant’s financial capability to provide the required level of care.
MIEMSS shall review each application submitted for completeness.

MIEMSS shall notify an applicant if an application is incomplete, and the applicant shall be afforded the opportunity to complete the application within 30 business days of the date of the notification.
As necessary, MIEMSS shall provide technical assistance to a hospital throughout the verification and designation process by answering questions about this subtitle and the designation process.
An applicant's designation application is the property of MIEMSS and is confidential information in accordance with:
Health Occupations Article, Title 1, Subtitle 4, and §14-506, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
General Provisions Article, Title 4, Subtitle 3, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: On-Site Review for Initial Trauma Center Designation.

para.text: After a hospital's application for designation has been accepted, MIEMSS shall conduct an on-site review of a hospital that has applied to be a Primary Adult Resource Center, or a Level I, II, or III trauma center.
On-Site Review Teams.
MIEMSS shall establish multidisciplinary on-site review teams composed of individuals knowledgeable in trauma care and systems.
The composition of the team shall be appropriate for the level of designation sought.
For trauma center designation, MIEMSS shall select a team which, at a minimum, shall include MIEMSS staff and representatives from three of the following categories:
Trauma surgeon;
Emergency physician;
Trauma nurse coordinator;
Administrator.
A staff person from MIEMSS shall accompany and coordinate the functions of the review team.
A team shall consist of professionals who do not have any conflict or competitive interest with the applicant.
If a hospital can demonstrate a reasonable basis for concern, MIEMSS shall consider allegations that conflicts of interest exist between an on-site reviewer and an applicant.
Contact with Members of On-Site Review Team.

Except as authorized by MIEMSS, an applicant's administration, faculty, medical staff, employees, and representatives may not have any contact with an on-site review team member relating to the review process after the team members are announced and before the on-site review is conducted.
A violation of §B(7)(a) of this regulation may be grounds for denial by MIEMSS of the hospital's application.
The on-site review team shall:
Evaluate the appropriateness and capability of the applicant to provide trauma care services, according to the designation standards described in COMAR 30.08.05;
Verify the hospital's ability to meet the:
Responsibilities of, and the resources, equipment, and performance standards for, the level of designation sought, and
Overall needs of the trauma system in that region;
Familiarize themselves with the hospital's application and the designation standards;
Inspect the hospital's physical plant;
Interview trauma team members and management personnel;
Examine the hospital's trauma-related documents, including patient care records;
Review other materials considered appropriate by MIEMSS;
Provide an exit interview of preliminary findings to the applicant upon completion of the on-site review; and
Provide a brief written summary of preliminary findings upon completion of the on-site review.
Confidentiality of On-Site Review Records.
MIEMSS shall require and maintain confidentiality of an on-site review record.
An on-site review record is confidential and exempt from public disclosure under General Provisions Article, Title 4, Subtitle 3, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Except as provided in Health Occupations Article, Title 1, Subtitle 4, Annotated Code of Maryland, an on-site review record is not discoverable or admissible in evidence.

A member of the on-site review team may not divulge, and may not be compelled to divulge, any information obtained or included in on-site review records submitted to MIEMSS relating to the on-site review, including in any civil action resulting from MIEMSS' designation process.

Notwithstanding §§A and B of this regulation, instead of conducting an on-site review, MIEMSS may take into consideration or coordinate with verification surveys by the American College of Surgeons or other specialty medical organizations.
As soon as practicable, but not later than 45 business days after completion of the on-site review, MIEMSS shall provide written notice to a hospital of its designation status.
MIEMSS may:
Designate the hospital as a trauma or specialty referral center as proposed by the applicant;

Designate the hospital at a level of designation lower than the applicant proposed, if the on-site review determined that the hospital does not meet the standards for the level of designation proposed;
Adjust the level of an applicant's designation based on system needs and the hospital's ability to meet those needs; or
Deny designation as a trauma center at any level or as a specialty referral center.
Provisional or Full Designation.

MIEMSS may initially designate a trauma or specialty referral center as provisional on the conditions and for the provisional period of 6 to 12 months, including any extensions that MIEMSS deems appropriate, but not to exceed 36 total months of provisional designation;
MIEMSS shall require each provisional trauma or specialty referral center to:
Have a written work plan to rectify deficiencies; and
Demonstrate progress on the work plan throughout the provisional period.
At the end of the provisional period, including any extensions, MIEMSS may:
Grant full designation to the trauma or specialty referral center; or
Deny the trauma or specialty referral center's designation under §D of this regulation.

MIEMSS may grant full designation to a hospital in full compliance with this chapter for a period not to exceed 3 years, excluding any extension during the reverification process as set forth in Regulation .10 of this chapter.
Denial of Designation. MIEMSS may deny a hospital's designation as a trauma or specialty referral center if it finds that the hospital:
Does not meet the requirements of this subtitle for the level of designation or specialty;
Has engaged in unauthorized contact with an on-site review team member, as prohibited by Regulation .05B(7) of this chapter;
Made a false statement or omitted a material fact in the hospital records, documentation, or materials required to be submitted that pertain to the designation process;
Is less qualified than another applicant hospital in the same geographic service area; or
Should not be designated for another relevant reason.
Notice of Denial of Designation.
MIEMSS shall issue a written notice of denial of designation to a hospital.
The notice of denial of designation shall conform to State Government Article, §10-207, Annotated Code of Maryland.
MIEMSS shall send the notice of denial of designation to the chief executive officer of the hospital.
MIEMSS shall notify the EMS Board of the action taken.

If MIEMSS approves a hospital's designation as a trauma or specialty referral center as proposed by the applicant, MIEMSS shall require the hospital to accept or decline the proposed designation within 30 business days from the date the hospital receives the notice.
A hospital may file an appeal with the EMS Board in accordance with Regulation .08 of this chapter if MIEMSS:
Approves the hospital at a level of designation lower than the applicant proposed;
Designates the hospital as provisional; or
Denies designation as a trauma center at any level or as a specialty center.
If the EMS Board overturns MIEMSS' decision, MIEMSS shall designate the hospital as a trauma or specialty referral center as directed by the EMS Board.
If the hospital does not timely appeal MIEMSS' decision, MIEMSS' decision is the final agency decision.

section.heading: Change in Designation Status of Trauma or Specialty Referral Center.

para.text: A designated trauma or specialty referral center:
Has the right to relinquish its designation as a trauma or specialty referral center or to request a designation lower than its current level of designation; and
Shall provide the Office of Care Integration with 90 calendar days advance written notice of its request to change its designation status.
If the designated trauma center applies for a lower level of designation, MIEMSS:
At its discretion, may repeat all or part of the designation process set forth in this chapter; and
Shall consider the request based upon the criteria described in Regulation .02 of this chapter.
Temporary Inability to Comply with Standards.

For an anticipated inability to comply with standards, a designated trauma or specialty referral center shall notify the Office of Care Integration at least 5 business days before it is temporarily unable to comply with the requirements for designated trauma or specialty centers as set forth in COMAR 30.08.03.

For an unanticipated or emergency inability to comply with standards, a designated trauma or specialty referral center shall notify the Emergency Medical Resource Center (EMRC), local EMS jurisdictions, and the Office of Care Integration immediately when it is temporarily unable to comply with the requirements for designated trauma or specialty centers as set forth in COMAR 30.08.02, and provide updates every 12 hours.
The notice shall be in writing and shall specify the reasons for and the anticipated duration of the temporary inability to comply with the standards.
MIEMSS shall determine whether the temporary inability to comply with the standards warrants corrective action under COMAR 30.08.13.
A designated trauma or specialty referral center may request to be designated at a higher level at any time, subject to the following:
A center’s requests must be a minimum of 24 months apart; and
In considering the request, MIEMSS shall proceed in accordance with Regulations .01—.08 of this chapter.

section.heading: Reverification of Trauma or Specialty Referral Center Designation.

para.text: A designated trauma or specialty referral center, other than a designated adult or pediatric burn center, shall repeat the designation process, as set forth in this chapter, every 3 years, or sooner if determined by MIEMSS, and as communicated to the hospital as the term of designation.
MIEMSS may reverify a center for less than 3 years if it determines based on its assessment that a shorter reverification cycle is appropriate.
The planned duration of a center’s designation shall be communicated to the hospital at the beginning of the period.

A designated adult or pediatric burn center, if verified by the American Burn Association, shall concurrently submit to MIEMSS the application submitted to the American Burn Association, along with such supplements as may be required by MIEMSS to demonstrate compliance with COMAR 30.08.06, and notify MIEMSS immediately of any change in its verification status.
At MIEMSS’ discretion:
MIEMSS may accept verification of a trauma or specialty referral center by a nationally recognized medical specialty organization in lieu of conducting an on-site reverification review;

MIEMSS may determine that there is sufficient data available to MIEMSS concerning the ongoing operation of the trauma or specialty center so that an on-site review is not necessary for a determination of reverification; or

MIEMSS may conduct an on-site review for reverification with MIEMSS staff and representatives, if any, from among the categories required for an initial designation site-review team as MIEMSS deems appropriate.
If a designated trauma or specialty referral center is in good standing:

MIEMSS shall send written notice to the chief executive officer of the trauma or specialty referral center requesting that the trauma or specialty referral center submit, within 60 calendar days, a request for reverification of its designation status; and
The designated trauma or specialty referral center shall retain its current designation status until the reverification process is completed.
At the time of the reverification process, MIEMSS shall publish a notice in the Maryland Register that:
Lists the trauma and specialty referral centers that have requested reverification of their designation status;

Requests a person with knowledge of any reason why a designated trauma or specialty referral center should not have its designation status reverified to submit a written statement of the reason to MIEMSS within 20 business days following publication of the notice; and

Requests that a hospital not designated that wishes to be considered for designation as a trauma or specialty referral center submit a written application to the Office of Care Integration in accordance with Regulation .03 of this chapter within 60 calendar days following publication of the notice.

section.heading: Designated Thrombectomy-Capable Primary Stroke Center.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11, a designated thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center hospital shall:

para.text: Be designated by MIEMSS as a primary stroke center at the time of application for designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Continue to meet the primary stroke center requirements in COMAR 30.08.11 to the extent such requirements are consistent with designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;

Require each physician who performs mechanical thrombectomy to have performed 15 mechanical thrombectomies over the past 12 months or 30 over the past 24 months. The total volume of cases may include procedures performed at other facilities;
Have performed mechanical thrombectomy and have provided post-procedure care for a minimum of 15 patients in the past 12 months or at least 30 patients over the past 24 months;
Meet the requirements of Regulations .01—.15 of this chapter; and
Meet the requirements for a site review in COMAR 30.08.02.06, which may be satisfied by completing either:
An on-site review by MIEMSS; or
A site survey as part of The Joint Commission Disease Specific Care Certification Program for certification as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center if the hospital:

Authorizes The Joint Commission to provide MIEMSS with survey findings, certification reports, and other information related to The Joint Commission’s certification of the hospital as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Allows MIEMSS to participate in the accreditation and certification site; and
Provides MIEMSS any additional information required to determine that the hospital has satisfied the requirements for designation under this chapter.

section.heading: Organization.
section.text: The hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.02.

section.heading: Emergency Department.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.03.

section.heading: Operating Room.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.04.

section.heading: Stroke Team.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.05.

section.heading: Intensive Care Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall maintain an intensive care unit that:

para.text: Has designated beds for the care of the acute stroke patient;
Has at all times on-site practitioners with critical care privileges (e.g., Attending Physicians, APNs, PAs, Fellows, or Residents);
Provides care to acute stroke patients by qualified clinical staff who meet the requirements in Regulation .11 of this chapter;
Follows standardized processes derived from evidence-based clinical practice guidelines to facilitate clinical care;
Incorporates individualized plans of care that are based on the patient’s assessed needs and that reflect coordination of care with other programs, as determined by patient comorbidities;
Has a process to assess the abilities and resources of family members to be involved in post-acute care; and
Maintains written documentation delineating the function of the intensive care unit, including:
Admission criteria;
Discharge criteria;
Acute stroke care protocols;
Interdisciplinary rounding;
Rehabilitation assessment and services in the hospital; and
Outcome data.

section.heading: Stroke Unit.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.07.

section.heading: Laboratory/Diagnostic Services.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.08.

section.heading: Neuroimaging Services.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.09, the hospital shall have the following diagnostic capability available when indicated:

para.text: Carotid duplex ultrasound;
Transcranial ultrasonography; and
Transesophageal/transthoracic echocardiogram.

section.heading: Endovascular Interventional Services.
section.text: A hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall have:

para.text: Interventional services promptly available at all times with appropriately trained support staff and necessary equipment;
Interventional services that include:
Intra-arterial reperfusion therapy; and
Stenting/angioplasty of intracranial vessels;

A neurointerventionalist who may be a Board-certified/Board-eligible neuroradiologist, neurologist, or neurosurgeon with hospital credential privileges on-call with a 30-minute arrival time to the hospital; and
Written procedures or protocols demonstrating the ability to simultaneously meet the emergency needs of multiple complex stroke patients, including assessment and appropriate treatment.

section.heading: Qualifications of Stroke Center Director and Clinicians.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.10, qualifications for a neurointerventionalist include performance of 15 mechanical thrombectomies over the past 12 months or 30 over the past 24 months:

section.heading: Qualifications of Emergency Department Clinical Staff.
section.text: The hospital shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.11.

section.heading: Prevention/Public Education.
section.text: The hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall meet the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.12.

section.heading: Policies, Protocols, Guidelines, and Agreements.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.11.13, a hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall:

para.text: Have written policies ensuring that:
Transfer of patients from another facility is appropriate and patients are received in a timely manner; and
All stroke patients will receive medical care commensurate with the hospital’s designation as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center;
Have written procedures demonstrating the ability to care for simultaneous complex interventional radiology stroke patients using appropriate clinical staff;
Have written care protocols for advanced treatment of complex stroke patients, including, but not limited to, acute ischemic stroke patients and acute intra-arterial therapeutic interventions; and

Document and review the scope of practice and the roles and responsibilities of nurse practitioners and physician assistants providing care to the acute stroke patient in the intensive care unit, the emergency department, and the stroke unit.

section.heading: Quality Management.
section.text: In addition to meeting the requirements of COMAR 30.08.14, a hospital designated as a thrombectomy-capable primary stroke center shall:

para.text: Monitor and demonstrate 24-hour post-procedure stroke and death rates of less than or equal to 1 percent for diagnostic neuro-angiography;
Monitor documentation of the reasons potentially eligible ischemic stroke patients did not receive mechanical thrombectomy;

In cases where mechanical endovascular reperfusion therapy is appropriate, achieve door-to-device times, arrival to first pass of thrombectomy device, in 50 percent or more of eligible acute ischemic stroke patients within 90 minutes for direct arriving patients and within 60 minutes for inter-facility transfer patients treated with endovascular therapy; and
Demonstrate progress towards reducing arrival to first pass of thrombectomy device to within 90 minutes for 75 percent or more of eligible acute ischemic stroke patients who arrive directly.

container.heading: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund

para.text: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund is a special, non-lapsing fund established under Public Safety Article, §3-206.1, Annotated Code of Maryland, for the purpose of providing funding to support activities and training by the Commission.
This chapter establishes the procedures and authorizations for the use of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Commission” means the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
“Department” means the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Executive Director” means the Executive Director of the Police and Correctional Training Commissions, or a designee.
“Fund” means the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund.
“Staff” means employees of the Police and Correctional Training Commissions.
The Fund shall receive an annual appropriation pursuant to Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, §7-301, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Fund is not subject to State Finance and Procurement Article, §7-302, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Interest earnings shall be credited to the Fund.
The State Treasurer shall hold the Fund separately, and the State Comptroller shall account for the Fund.
The Fund may only be used to provide funding to the Commission.

section.heading: Use and Administration of the Fund.

para.text: The Fund shall only be used in support of the Commission’s general powers and duties under Public Safety Article, §§3-206.1, 3-207, and 3-208, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Commission, in coordination with the Executive Director, shall:
Establish goals, objectives, and an annual spending plan that supports the duties and responsibilities of the Commission and training needs for law enforcement;
Review and approve proposed expenditures; and
Ensure that each approved expenditure is consistent with Public Safety Article, §3-207, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Executive Director is responsible for fiscal oversight of the Fund.
Staff shall assist the Executive Director with the development of an annual spending plan that is consistent with the Commission’s strategic plan and specific training goals.
The Department will provide administrative staff support to process procurement and fiscal transactions related to the Commission’s approved fund expenditures.
The Executive Director shall provide quarterly updates to the Commission on fund expenditures and initiatives.
Money expended from the Fund is not intended to take the place of funding that would otherwise be appropriated to the Department or Police and Correctional Training Commissions.

para.text: An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8–303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.
If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to:
Complete the application; and
Provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board in §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application:
Shall be considered abandoned; and
May be destroyed.
Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking licensure shall:
Submit a new application;
Meet all of the requirements for licensure; and
Pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.
The Board shall place the license of any registered nurse or licensed practical nurse on inactive status if the licensee:

Has not satisfactorily completed 1,000 hours of active nursing practice or graduated from an approved nursing program within the 5-year period immediately preceding the date of anticipated renewal or chooses inactive status;
Completes the biennial application for inactive status; and
Pays all fees.

A licensee on inactive status may not practice nursing in this State. However, a registered nurse on inactive status may use the title “registered nurse”, and a practical nurse on inactive status may use the title “licensed practical nurse”.
A licensee on inactive status may apply for an active status license provided that the licensee:
Meets the renewal requirements of Health Occupations Article, §8-312, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Submits to the Board:
The required application; and
Written, verified evidence that the licensee has submitted to a criminal history records check in accordance with Regulation .13 of this chapter by:
Submitting one complete set of fingerprints required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
Paying all fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
An additional fee may not be charged to change from inactive to active status.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the Board of Nursing.

“Board-approved course” means an educational offering specific to the case management of the injured worker under the Workers' Compensation Commission which meets the criteria established by the Board.
“Central Repository” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
“Commission” means the Workers' Compensation Commission.
“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
Medical Case Management.

“Medical case management” means any type of contact, including electronic, written, and personal, with the injured worker, for the purpose of the planning and coordination of health services appropriate to achievement of medical rehabilitation of the injured worker.
“Medical case management” includes but is not limited to:
Case assessment;
Implementation and coordination of services with the injured worker, family, and health care providers;
Evaluation of treatment results;
Coordinating community re-entry;
Return to work with the employer of injury; and
Referral for further vocational rehabilitation services.
“Medical claims consultant” means a registered nurse who consults on medical aspects of an injured worker's rehabilitation without any contact with the injured worker.
“Multistate licensure privilege” has the meaning set forth in COMAR 10.27.01.01B.
“Registered nurse (RN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice registered nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing.
“RN-WCCM” means a registered nurse-workers' compensation medical case manager.
For certification as an RN-WCCM, an applicant shall:
Hold a current license to practice registered nursing in this State or a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing;
Submit documentation of successful completion of a Board-approved course;
Submit to the Board a completed application for certification as an RN-WCCM;
Pay all fees; and
Submit to a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Board shall include on the RN's license the designation WCCM.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant from out-of-State shall meet the requirements as stated in this regulation.
Unless renewed biennially, a certification to practice as an RN-WCCM expires at the same time as the registered nurse license.
Before certification as an RN-WCCM expires, the RN-WCCM may renew the certification for an additional term, if the RN—WCCM:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Has practiced a minimum of 2,000 hours in the past 2 years as an RN—WCCM;
Submits a completed application for renewal on the form the Board requires;
Pays all fees; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §E of this regulation, submits written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.

If the registered nurse does not meet the practice requirement stated in §B(2) of this regulation, the registered nurse shall complete a Board-approved course to be eligible for renewal of the RN-WCCM certification.
Upon notification by the Board that a CHRC is required before the certification can be renewed, a renewal applicant shall comply with all of the requirements under §B of this regulation.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certification holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month.
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month; and
In 2037— all applicants with an August or September birth month.

For renewal applicants who are required to submit a CHRC, the Board may not renew a certification without written documentation that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Exceptions.
section.text: This chapter does not apply to an individual who:

para.text: Other than a certified nursing assistant, practices a health occupation, that the individual is authorized to practice under the Health Occupations Article, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Provides for the gratuitous care of friends, domestic partners, or family members;
Performs nursing assistant tasks while a nursing student enrolled in an accredited nursing program if the individual either:
Is practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors; or

Successfully completed the portion of the approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements of an approved nursing assistant training program as described in Regulation .05D of this chapter;
Performs nursing assistant tasks:
While a student enrolled in an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program; and
While practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors;
Practices as a certified nursing assistant-I for less than 4 months in accordance with 42 CFR §483.35(d);
Performs nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse so long as the delegated nursing tasks do not become a routine part of the individual's job duties;
Performs nursing tasks delegated by an advanced practice registered nurse in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(d), Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Performs technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(e), Annotated Code of Maryland.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Acute care nursing assistant training program” means a course of training that meets the acute care nursing assistant training program curriculum approved by the Board.
“Board” means the Maryland Board of Nursing.
“Central Repository” means the Maryland Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Certificate” means a certificate issued by the Board to practice as a certified nursing assistant in the State.
Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” means an individual, regardless of title, who, for compensation and subject to regulations adopted by the Board, routinely performs:
Nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or advanced practice registered nurse; or
Technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife.
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” does not include dialysis technician or medication technician.
Certified Nursing Assistant-I (CNA-I).
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” means a CNA who:
Meets the requirements set by the Board and federal law; and
May practice in any practice setting.
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” includes a:
CNA who was certified as a geriatric nursing assistant on March 31, 2026;
Certified medicine aide; and
CNA who is certified under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05(c)(5), Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Certified nursing assistant-II (CNA-II)” means a CNA who:
On March 31, 2026, was certified as a CNA but not certified as a geriatric nursing assistant; and
May not practice in a nursing facility or skilled nursing facility.

“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” means the performance of both a State criminal history records check by the Central Repository and a national criminal history records check performed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

“Criminal history record information” means information provided by the criminal history records check regarding an applicant’s criminal arrests, charges, and convictions and other dispositions of criminal charges.
“Good standing” means without an encumbrance that limits or restricts practice, such as revocation, suspension, or probation.
“Nursing assistant competency evaluation” means an examination approved by the Board that:
Determines the competency of the individual to practice as a CNA-I; and
Meets the requirements under federal law.
“Nursing assistant training program” means a course of training approved by the Board that meets the requirements under federal and State law.
“Service member” has the meaning stated in State Government Article, §9-901, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Temporary nurse aide” means an individual who practiced as a geriatric nursing assistant without certification during the national Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Public Health Emergency, as declared on January 31, 2020, and periodically continued by the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services, pursuant to the waiver of the requirements of 42 CFR §483.35(d) issued by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services on March 6, 2020.
“Technical task” means a routine clinical act or task that does not require clinical judgment and is performed with the supervision as specified in COMAR 10.69.02.
“Temporary nurse aide training” means an 8-hour online training and examination program offered by:
The American Health Care Association;
The National Center for Assisted Living; or
Another comparable program approved by the Board.
Fees are as follows:
Initial certification fee — $20;
Endorsement fee — $20;
Renewal fee — $40;
Verification of certification to another jurisdiction — $25;
Returned check fee — $25;
Duplicate certificate fee — $10.
Fees are not refundable.
An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under §A(2) of this regulation;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) of this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.

If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to complete the application and provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board under §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application shall be considered abandoned and may be destroyed.

Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking CNA certification shall submit a new application on the form required by the Board and meet all of the requirements for CNA certification and pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.
Initial Certification. An applicant for initial nursing assistant certification shall have successfully:
Completed:
An approved nursing assistant training program;
An approved acute care nursing assistant training program;
A portion of an approved nursing education program that has been determined by the Board to meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

Service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §1-702, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Passed a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Hold a certificate to practice as a nursing assistant that:

Was issued by another state or territory of the United States that has certification requirements that are essentially similar to those set forth in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Is in good standing; and
Have successfully completed a nursing assistant training program that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Any applicant for nursing assistant certification may not have:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-10, Annotated Code of Maryland; or

A record of abuse, negligence, or misappropriation of a client's property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any other state or territory of the United States against the certification of the CNA.
Nursing Education Programs.
To meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board, a portion of a nursing education program must include courses with content that primarily focuses on:
Nursing fundamentals;
Mental health;
Health assessment;
Nursing ethics; and
The content listed under 42 CFR §483.152(b).

If a portion of a nursing education program does not include courses with content that primarily focuses on the subject matters set forth in § D(1) of this regulation, the Board may review and approve other equivalent subject matters as meeting the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-1 shall meet the qualifications set forth in §A of this regulation.
Temporary Nurse Aides.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall be deemed to have completed a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board if the temporary nurse aide:
Completed a temporary nurse aide training course;
Completed a minimum of 100 hours of on-the-job training as a temporary nurse aide that:
Met the requirements under 42 CFR §483.152(a) and 42 CFR §483.152(b)(2)—(7); and
Was not provided in a facility described under 42 CFR §483.151(b)(2)—(3); and
In addition to the minimum 100 hours of on-the-job training, worked as a temporary nurse aide competently for a minimum of 160 hours.

A temporary nurse aide whose on-the-job training did not meet all of the requirements under 42 CFR 483.152(a) and 42 CFR 483.152(b)(2)—(7) may receive supplemental training in those requirements and be deemed to meet the requirement of §F(1)(b)(i) of this regulation.
Initial Certification.
An applicant for initial certification shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit to the Board one of the items in §A(2) of this regulation.
Verification Requirements.

For graduates of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program, an application that has been signed by the program coordinator or faculty of the training program completed by the applicant;

For service members, documentation demonstrating successful completion of service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board;

For nursing students and graduates, an official transcript demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

For foreign-educated nursing graduates, a copy of an evaluation of the applicant’s transcript through a Board-approved vendor demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A program coordinator or faculty of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program:
May sign an application before graduation; and
Shall submit written verification, as required by the Board, of program completion to the Board after 5 business days of the applicant’s program completion.

An applicant shall submit an application for initial certification after 24 months of the date of completion of an approved nursing assistant training program, an approved acute care nursing assistant training program, or portion of an approved nursing education program.

If an applicant fails to meet §A(4) of this regulation, an applicant still seeking certification shall take or re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program and comply with §A(4) of this regulation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit the following verifications directly to the Board from the appropriate authority:
A certificate to practice as a nursing assistant in good standing from another state or territory with certification requirements that are essentially similar to the requirements in this State; and
A certificate of completion from a nursing assistant training program in that state or territory that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Every applicant shall attest on the application whether the applicant has:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification; and

A record of abuse, neglect, or misappropriation of a client’s property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any state or territory of the United States against the certification of the applicant.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-I shall:
Submit an application to the Board on the form required by the Board; and
Comply with §§A(1)(c) and A(3)—(5) of this regulation.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall:
Comply with §A of this regulation; and
Ensure that the administrator, director of nursing, or human resources representative of the applicant’s employer submits to the Board an attestation, on the form required by the Board, that:
Is completed by the:
Applicant;
Registered Nurse instructor or supervisor of the applicant during employment; and
Administrator or director of nursing for the employer; and
Verifies that the applicant satisfies the requirements of Regulation .05F of this chapter.
An individual is eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation if the individual:
Meets the education requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter; or
Must retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation in order to renew or reinstate a certification in accordance with Regulation .10C(2)(a) of this chapter.

Except for service members, an individual shall sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter.

An individual who fails to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational qualifications must re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program in order to be eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Re-testing.
An individual who fails to obtain a passing score on the first examination may retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation three additional times.
An individual shall wait at least 45 calendar days from the date of the prior evaluation before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.

An individual who fails to obtain a passing score after taking a nursing assistant competency evaluation four times must complete a new approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
The Board may issue a temporary practice certificate to an applicant who:
Has met the appropriate certification requirements to the satisfaction of the Board;
Does not have a criminal record; and
Has not been the subject of a health professional disciplinary action in this State or another jurisdiction.
Unless the Board suspends or revokes a temporary practice certificate, the temporary practice certificate expires 90 calendar days after the date of issuance.
A temporary practice certificate may be extended up to an additional 90 calendar days if the applicant is awaiting the completion of the criminal history records check.
The Board may not issue a certificate to an applicant until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history record information of the applicant; and
Approved the application.

Unless subject to discipline, the Board shall issue a certificate to each applicant who meets all the requirements of this chapter and Health Occupations Article, §§8-6A-05 and 8-6A-06, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Expiration.
Unless renewed for an additional two-year term, and except as otherwise provided in §A(2) of this regulation, a certificate expires in accordance with the following schedule:
The certificate of a certificate holder with an odd-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an odd-numbered year; and
The certificate of a certificate holder with an even-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an even-numbered year.
A certificate shall not expire within 180 calendar days of the date of issuance.
Renewal Notice.
At least 3 months before a certificate expires, the Board shall send the certificate holder a renewal notice by either:
First-class mail to the last known address of the certificate holder; or
Electronic means to the last known electronic address of the certificate holder.
The renewal notice shall provide:
The date on which the certificate holder’s certificate is scheduled to expire;

The date by which the Board must receive a renewal application in order for a certificate to remain active until the renewal application submitted by the certificate holder is processed by the Board, in accordance with State Government Article, §10-226(b), Annotated Code of Maryland;
The amount of the renewal fee; and
If the certificate holder is required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §D of this regulation:
Notice that the certificate holder must submit to a CHRC in order to renew the certificate; and
Written instructions for how to complete a CHRC.
It is the responsibility of the certificate holder to:
Be aware of the expiration date of the certificate; and
Renew the certificate before it expires.
Failure of a certificate holder to receive the renewal notice sent by the Board does not relieve the certificate holder of the responsibility to renew a certificate before it expires.
Renewal Requirements.
The Board shall renew a certificate if the individual applying for renewal:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Submits a complete application for renewal on the form required by the Board;
Pays the renewal fee;

Provides satisfactory evidence, as required by the Board, of16 hours of active employment, for compensation, as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration or meet the requirements under §C(2) of this regulation; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with § D of this regulation, complies with the requirements of Regulation .04A of this chapter.
If the individual applying for renewal does not have 16 hours of active employment as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration the individual shall:
If a CNA-I, take and pass a nursing assistant competency evaluation; or
If a CNA-II, complete a nursing assistant training program..
Schedule for CHRCs. CHRCs for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certificate holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2025 — all applicants with an August or September birth month;
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month; and
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month.
Grace Period. A certificate holder has a 30 calendar day grace period beyond the expiration date of the certificate to renew the certificate.

The Board shall reinstate the certificate of a certificate holder who has failed to renew the certificate for any reason, if the certificate holder meets the renewal requirements in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-08, Annotated Code of Maryland, and Regulation .10 of this chapter.
An applicant for administrative reinstatement who has failed to renew the certificate for a period of 1 year or more shall submit to a CHRC before the certificate is reinstated.
