para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the Maryland Board of Nursing.
“Central Repository” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.39.01.02.
“Certificate” means a certificate issued by the Board to practice as a certified medication technician in this State.
Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” means an individual, regardless of title, who:
Routinely performs delegated nursing tasks which were delegated by a registered nurse (RN) or licensed practice nurse (LPN) for compensation; and
Is certified under COMAR 10.39.01.
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” does not include:
A medication technician; or
An individual who merely provides assistance with activities of daily living unless the client's needs are such that adverse health consequences are predictable.
“Clinical refresher course” means a course of study approved by the Board to maintain the medication technician's knowledge and skill to administer medication.
“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.39.01.02.
“Licensed practical nurse (LPN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice licensed practical nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice licensed practical nursing.
“Medication technician (MT)” means an individual who:
Has successfully completed a Board-approved MT training program;
Meets any other qualifications set by the Board; and
Is certified by the Board as a MT.

“Medication technician training program” means a course of training approved by the Board that meets the basic MT core curriculum and content training specific to the setting in which the MT will work.
“Multistate licensure privilege” has the meaning set forth in COMAR 10.27.01.01B.
“Registered nurse (RN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice registered nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing.
An applicant for MT certification shall:
Be 18 years old or older; and
Submit to the Board:
An application to the Board on the form required by the Board and signed by the RN that taught the applicant's medication technician training program; and
The required fee;
Be of good moral character; and
Submit to a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.
An applicant for MT certification may not have:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification under this subtitle; or

A record of abuse, negligence, misappropriation of a resident's property, or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any state or territory of the United States against any certificate or license issued to the applicant.
An applicant for MT certification from any other state, territory, or country shall meet all requirements of this chapter.
An applicant for MT certification shall provide:

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under §A(4) of this regulation;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form;
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §D(1) of this section is incomplete or insufficient.

The Board shall renew the certificate of each certificate holder who meets the requirements of this chapter.
The certificate holder shall renew the certificate every 2 years by birth month.
At least 3 months before a certificate expires, the Board shall send the certificate holder a renewal notice by:
First-class mail to the last known address of the certificate holder; or
Electronic means to the last known electronic address of the certificate holder.
An individual applying for renewal of certification shall provide evidence of:
Satisfactory completion of a Board-approved clinical refresher course;
Completion of 100 hours of practice as a certified medicine technician within the 2-year period preceding the date of renewal;
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §F of this regulation, submission to a CHRC by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
Upon notification by the Board that a CHRC is required before the certificate can be renewed, a renewal application shall comply with all the requirements under D of this regulation.

The Board shall reinstate the certificate of a certificate holder who has failed to renew the certificate for any reason, if the certificate holder meets the renewal requirements in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-08, Annotated Code of Maryland and Regulation .05 of this chapter.

An applicant eligible for the national theory exam will be notified by the Board as to when the applicant may schedule the theory exam.
To be eligible for licensure, an applicant shall earn a score of:
75 percent or higher on the theory examination; and
75 percent or higher on the clinical examination.
A license may not be issued until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history records information; and
Approved the application.
Term. A license issued pursuant to Health Occupations Article, §8-6B-12, Annotated Code of Maryland, authorizes the licensee to practice licensed electrology while the license is active.

Expiration. Unless renewed, a license expires on the 28th day of a licensee's birth month of every odd-numbered year, except that an initial license shall not expire within 180 days of the date of issuance.

The applicable fee as set forth in COMAR 10.53.12; and

The licensee is otherwise entitled to be licensed; and

Evidence of completion of 10 CEUs for each year before application;
The renewal fee as set forth in COMAR 10.53.12; and

Facsimile machine, photocopier, and scanner for copying; and
Computer.

“Licensed direct-entry midwife” does not include a licensed registered nurse certified as a nurse-midwife under Health Occupations Article, Title 8, Annotated Code of Maryland.

A woman’s newborn for the purpose of perinatal or postpartum care.

section.heading: Term and Renewal of License and Reinstatement of License.

para.text: A license issued under this regulation authorizes the licensee to practice direct-entry midwifery while the license is active.
A license:
Expires on the 28th day of a licensee's birth month of every odd-numbered year, except that an initial license shall not expire within 180 days of the date of issuance;
Is valid for 2 years, except for an initial license issued before the next renewal date;
Issued for less than the full 2-year period shall be renewed at the next annual renewal date; and
May be renewed for an additional term if the applicant:
Meets the renewal requirements under §B(4)(c) of this regulation:
Pays to the Board a renewal fee specified in Regulation 18 of this chapter; and
Submits to the Board:
A renewal application on the form that the Board requires; and
Satisfactory evidence of compliance with any continuing education or other competency requirements for license renewal.
In addition to all other qualifications and requirements established by the Board for license renewal, the renewal applicant shall submit proof of completion of:
20 accredited and Board-approved continuing education units to be completed in the 2 years preceding the renewal date;
4 hours of peer review in the 2 years before the renewal date in accordance with NARM standards for official peer review; and
Submission of the annual reports required under Regulation .12 of this chapter.
The Board shall renew the license of each licensee who meets the requirements of this regulation.
A renewal applicant shall be placed on inactive status if the licensee:
Fails to provide satisfactory evidence of compliance with any continuing education requirements under this regulation for license renewal; or
Fails to submit the annual report required under Regulation .12 of this chapter.
If the renewal applicant fails to submit the required documents within 1 year of the renewal date, the status of the license shall be changed to nonrenewed.
The Board shall place a licensee on inactive status at the request of the licensee if the licensee submits to the Board:
A completed application for inactive status on the form required by the Board; and
The fee for inactive status specified in Regulation .18 of this chapter.
The Board shall reactivate the license of a licensee who has requested inactive status if the licensee:
Complies with any continuing education and data reporting requirements established by the Board for this purpose;
Pays to the Board a reactivation fee specified in Regulation .18 of this chapter; and
Is otherwise entitled to be licensed in accordance with this regulation.
The Board shall reinstate the license of an individual who has failed to renew the license for any reason if the individual:
Is otherwise entitled to be licensed in accordance with this regulation;
Complies with any continuing education and data reporting requirements established by the Board for this purpose;
Submits a completed application for reinstatement to the Board;
Pays to the Board the fee for reinstatement;
Completes a criminal history record check in accordance with Heath Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland, for a license that has expired or lapsed for more than 1 year; and
Applies to the Board for reinstatement of the license within 5 years after the license expires.

The Board may not reinstate the license of a licensed direct-entry midwife who fails to apply for reinstatement of the license within 5 years after the license expires. The individual may become licensed by meeting the current requirements for obtaining a new license as set forth in:
Health Occupations Article, §§8-6C-13 — 8-6C-16, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
This chapter.

A licensee shall submit to an additional criminal history records check every 12 years. The Board may not renew a license if the criminal history record information required by this section has not been received.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the licensee’s birth month as follows:
In 2027 — all applicants with a September and October birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a November and December birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a January and February birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with a March and April birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a May and June birth month; and
In 2037 — all applicants with a July and August birth month.

section.heading: Requirements for Application for Initial Licensure.

para.text: An applicant for initial licensure as a certified midwife shall submit to the Board:

Shall be considered abandoned; and
May be destroyed.

Meet all of the requirements for licensure; and
Pay the required fees in accordance with Regulation .13 of this chapter in effect at the time of re-application.
A license issued under this regulation authorizes the licensee to practice licensed certified midwifery while the license is active.
Unless renewed, a license expires on the 28th day of a licensee's birth month of every odd-numbered year, except that an initial license shall not expire within 180 days of the date of issuance.
Before a license expires, the licensed certified midwife may renew the license for an additional 2-year term if the licensed certified midwife:
Is otherwise entitled to be licensed;
Pays to the Board the renewal fee specified in Regulation .13 of this chapter; and
Submits to the Board:
A renewal application on the form that the Board requires;
Satisfactory evidence of current national certification as a certified midwife by AMCB; and
If required to submit to a criminal history records check in accordance with § C of this regulation, evidence of submission to a criminal history records check as required by the Board.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the licensee’s birth month as follows:
In 2027 — all applicants with a September and October birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a November and December birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a January and February birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with a March and April birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a May and June birth month; and
In 2037 — all applicants with a July and August birth month.
The Board may grant a 30-day extension beyond a license’s expiration date so that the license may be renewed before it expires.

section.heading: Purpose and Scope.
section.text: This chapter:

para.text: Defines the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund;
Sets forth the responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Health with respect to the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund;
Describes the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission;
Identifies eligible applicants for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund; and
Outlines the grant process for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Administrative expenses” means staffing costs, costs associated with establishing and maintaining the Commission, and costs associated with the development, review, evaluation, and award of grants.
Applicant.
“Applicant” means an organization who applies to receive a grant under the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
“Applicant” includes an authorized representative acting on behalf of, or submitting an application on behalf of, an organization.

“Applied research” means research that is focused on determining how the research enterprise can most effectively translate existing scientific information into solutions to real-world problems, including new diagnostics and therapies for diseases.
“Basic research” means experimental or theoretical work undertaken to acquire new knowledge or understanding of cancer.
“Capital expenditures” means money spent to add or expand property, equipment, and assets that will benefit a grantee in the long term.
“Clinical research” means research:
Conducted primarily on patients; and
Designed to answer questions about the etiology, prevention, early detection, diagnosis, or treatment of cancer.
“Commission” means the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission as established in Health-General Article, §20-121, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Community-based participatory research” means a collaborative, partnership approach to research that equitably involves community members, organizational representatives, and researchers in all aspects of the research process.
“Department” means the Maryland Department of Health.
Educational Institution.
“Educational institution” means an organization whose primary mission is to educate individuals.
“Educational institution” includes:
Colleges;
Universities; and
Graduate schools.
“Fund” means the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
Grant.
“Grant” means financial assistance from the State to support an applicant's activities related to pediatric cancer research.
“Grant” does not mean a contract.
“Grantee” means an organization who receives a grant under the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
“Hospital” means an institution that is licensed in the State under COMAR 10.07.01 or other applicable standards established by the jurisdiction or state in which the service is provided.

“Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund” means the program which is administered by the Department under Health-General Article, §20-120, Annotated Code of Maryland, to provide grants to nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations to conduct pediatric cancer research.
“Nonprofit organization” means an organization that is classified under §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code as a nonprofit organization.
Research.
“Research” means activities to develop or advance the understanding of cancer or the techniques or modalities effective in the prevention, cure, screening, diagnosis, or treatment of cancer.
“Research” includes applied, basic, clinical, translational, and community-based participatory research.
“Secretary” means the Secretary of the Maryland Department of Health.
“State-based childhood cancer organization” means a social organization as defined by State Finance and Procurement Article, §7-402(a), Annotated Code of Maryland that:
Is headquartered in the State; and
Has a primary mission to address childhood cancer.
“Translational research” means using or applying new discoveries to benefit patient care.
The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund is a non-lapsing, special fund created by Health-General Article, §20-120, Annotated Code of Maryland, for pediatric cancer research, which is generated from:
Money appropriated in the State Budget to the Fund; and
Any other donations to the Fund.
Department Expenditure of Fund. The Department may only expend funds:
In accordance with an appropriation approved by the General Assembly in the annual State budget; or
Through an approved budget amendment under State Finance and Procurement Article, §§7-209 and 7-210, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Approved Utilization of the Fund. The Fund shall be used only:
To make grants for pediatric cancer research;
For administrative expenses; and

To distribute to a promotional account to be allocated to a State-based childhood cancer organization to be used to promote further donations to the Fund and to educate the State scientific community about opportunities for childhood cancer research through the Fund.
Each fiscal year, the Secretary may distribute and use no more than a total of 5 percent of the Fund for the purposes referenced in §C(2) and (3) of this regulation.
Any unspent portions of the Fund shall remain in the Fund and may not revert to the General Fund of the State.
Money expended from the Fund is supplemental to, and is not intended to take the place of, funding that would otherwise be appropriated to the Department for pediatric cancer research.

section.heading: Responsibilities of the Department.
section.text: The Department shall:

para.text: Administer the Fund;
Submit a report annually to the General Assembly on administration of the Fund;
Each fiscal year, decide on the amount from the Fund to be distributed to:
The promotional account;
Administrative expenses; and
Pediatric cancer research grants; and
Use the Fund to implement activities related to:
The promotional account;
Administrative expenses; and
Pediatric cancer research grants.

section.heading: Responsibilities of the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission.

para.text: The Commission oversees the award of competitive grants from the Fund.
Duties of the Commission. The Commission shall:
Develop the criteria, standards, and requirements for the review of applications for pediatric cancer research grants from the Fund;
Establish procedures and guidelines to be used in the review, evaluation, ranking, and rating of the research grant proposals;
Develop criteria and a process for reviewing grant applications to ensure that each application is complete and satisfies the criteria, standards, and requirements developed by the Commission;
Develop disclosure and recusal guidelines to be followed by members of the Commission when considering grant applications;
Ensure participation recusal is conducted in accordance with the guidelines required by §B(4) of this regulation;
Establish standards for the oversight of awards; and
Conduct progress reviews of grant recipients.
The Commission may consult with experts in performing its duties.

section.heading: Eligible Applicants for Pediatric Cancer Research Grants.

para.text: Subject to any limitations imposed under §B of this regulation, applicants eligible to receive grants from the Department under Regulation .04D(3) of this chapter include:
Nonprofit hospitals;
Educational institutions; and
Other nonprofit organizations the Department determines to be eligible.
The Department may limit the applicants eligible to receive a grant in §A of this regulation based on:
Availability of funds;
The Department's ability to account for and monitor the grant funding;
The qualifications of the applicants; or
The ability of the applicants to comply with requirements of the grant.

section.heading: Allowable Uses of the Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funds.
section.text: Funds granted for pediatric cancer research under Regulation .04D(3) of this chapter may be used for:

para.text: Applied research;
Basic research;
Clinical research;
Community-based participatory research; or
Translational research.

section.heading: Unallowable Uses of Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funds.
section.text: A grantee may not use grant funds from the Fund to pay for:

para.text: Renovations;
Capital expenditures;
Institutional overhead expenses, organizational expenses, or charges that are not directly related to pediatric cancer research;
Expenses arising from community-based support services; or
Individual-level prevention, cure, screening, diagnosis, or treatment that is unrelated to a research project eligible for the Fund.

section.heading: Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funding and Application.

para.text: Each fiscal year, the Department:
Shall determine the amount of funding available for pediatric cancer research grants; and
May consider awarding funding for grant applications for pediatric cancer research.
The Department shall make available the grant application and its instructions.
An applicant may not apply for grant funding for more than 2 years with a single grant application.
An applicant shall submit the completed application packet to the Department by the due date provided by the Department to be eligible for award consideration.
Each Maryland educational institution shall be considered as a singular entity, including:
The University System of Maryland and University of Maryland Medical System, including all their campuses and health entities;

The Johns Hopkins University and Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions, including all their campuses and health entities, the Kennedy Krieger Institute, and the Lieber Institute for Brain Development; and
All subsidiaries and locations of any other organization.
As part of the application for a pediatric cancer research grant under §D of this regulation, an applicant shall attest that the applicant:
Will use grant funds solely in accordance with the grant requirements;
Will conduct the pediatric cancer research for which the grant is requested in the State;
Has the legal capacity and all necessary legal authority to incur the obligations related to the grant award; and
Will comply with all applicable State and federal laws.

section.heading: Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Application Review and Approval.

para.text: The Commission, to review the grant applications that are submitted for funding under the Fund, may:
Develop one or more review committees; or
Contract with one or more external peer review consultants.
If a review committee or external peer review consultant is used for the purposes described in §A of this regulation:
The review committee or external peer review consultant shall make a recommendation to the Commission about the merits, rank, and rating of each application; and
The Commission shall then evaluate the review committee or external consultant’s report of each application.
The Commission shall recommend to the Department which projects should be funded.
The Department shall make the final determination on funding grant applications.
Grantees shall be subject to progress reviews on a schedule set by the Department.
The Commission, to conduct progress reviews and make recommendations to the Department about each grantee’s progress, may:
Develop one or more review committees; or
Contract with one or more external peer review consultants.
The Commission shall recommend to the Department whether to continue providing grant funds to each grantee.
The Department shall make the final determination on whether to continue providing grant funds to each grantee.

A grantee may apply to the Department for a no-cost extension of the grant period for the award before the expiration of the grant period by submitting a written request for an extension to the Department.
In evaluating whether to recommend an extension of the grant period, the Commission:
Shall assess whether progress has been made on the grant project; and
May recommend to the Department that an extension be granted based on reports submitted under Regulation .13 of this chapter.
The Department shall consider the Commission’s recommendation regarding the request for an extension and may approve a no-cost grant extension for up to 1 year.

section.heading: Payments, Terms and Conditions of Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Awards, and Terminations.

para.text: If a financial or progress report required in §B or C of this regulation is overdue, the Department may withhold payment to the grantee until the report is submitted.
Financial Reports and Records.
A grantee shall:
Establish a separate account to track expenditures under the grant;
Maintain accurate records, including documentation of each transaction pertaining to the grant;
Submit to the Department invoices for payment by the deadline specified by the Department;

Submit to the Department a final financial expenditure report containing the signature of the financial officer or designee of the entity affiliated with the grant award by the deadline specified by the Department; and
Submit a refund of any unexpended funds by the deadline specified by the Department.

The Department may audit the accounts referenced in §B(1) of this regulation at any time up to 3 years from the date the final financial expenditure report is submitted under §B(1) of this regulation.
A grantee shall retain all records pertaining to a grant award for 3 years from the date the final financial expenditure report is submitted under §B(1) of this regulation.
In the case of an audit or litigation, the Department may extend the time period under §B(2) or (3) of this regulation until the completion of the audit or litigation.
Progress Reports.
A grantee shall submit to the Department:
An interim report describing the progress of the grant by the deadline specified by the Department; and
A comprehensive final report by the deadline specified by the Department.
The Commission shall conduct oversight and progress reviews of grant recipients using reports submitted to the Department, site visits, or any other mechanism to be determined by the Commission.
The Department shall keep research results confidential as required by Health-General Article, §§4-101—4-103, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Publication of Research.
A grantee who publishes results from activities shall include in the publication an acknowledgement with the text: “Supported in part with funds from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.”
A grantee shall provide the Department with a copy of any published article pertaining to the activities conducted under the grant.
Ownership of Equipment. A grantee:
Shall ensure that equipment purchased under a grant under this chapter is used for the sole purpose of the grant;
Shall keep an inventory of all equipment purchased; and
May not transfer the equipment to another entity without the written permission of the Department.
Termination.
The Secretary may terminate a grant:
If a grantee fails to comply with:
The requirements of this chapter; or
State, federal, and municipal laws applicable to the performance of research under the grant;
If a grantee fails to carry out the purposes for which the grant was awarded;
In compliance with a court order; or
At the request of the grantee.
The Department and the State may not be responsible for any expenses incurred by a grantee after cancellation of a grant.
The grantee shall return all unexpended funds to the Department within 60 calendar days of termination of a grant.
Compliance with Existing Laws. A grantee shall ensure that an activity conducted in the performance of the grant is in compliance with all State, federal, and local laws.
Liability.
A grantee is solely responsible for their actions pertaining to research conducted under a grant award; and
The State and the Department may not be liable for any claims, losses, liabilities, expenses, or damages arising from research conducted under a grant awarded under this chapter.
A grantee shall enter into a grant agreement with the Department.

para.text: In General.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated and as defined in the Act.
Any terms also appearing in the Internal Revenue Code have the meanings defined there as well.
Terms Defined.
“Act” means the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program established in Housing and Community Development Article, Title 6, Subtitle 4, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Approved project” means a project approved by the Department in accordance with Regulation .04 of this chapter.
“Business entity” means a person that:
Conducts or operates a trade or business in the State; and
Is subject to the:
State income tax on individuals or corporations;
Financial institution franchise tax;
Public service company franchise tax; or
Insurance premiums tax.
“Contribution” means a donation by a business entity or an individual of money, goods, or real property of at least $500 in value to an approved project.
“Department” means the Department of Housing and Community Development, a principal department of the State.
“Designated neighborhood conservation area” means a geographically defined area that has been designated a neighborhood conservation area under COMAR 05.17.03.
“Individual” has the meaning stated in Tax-General Article, §10-101, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Individual of limited income” means an individual whose income does not exceed the upper income limits established by the Secretary under Housing and Community Development Article, §4-212, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Internal Revenue Code” means the federal Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and the regulations promulgated under it.
“Nonprofit organization” means a not-for-profit corporation, foundation, or other legal entity that is exempt from federal income tax under §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.
“Program” means the Community Investment Tax Credit Program.
“Priority funding area” has the meaning stated in State Finance and Procurement Article, §5-7B-02, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Redevelopment assistance” means the expenditure of funds by nonprofit organizations for labor and materials used directly in the physical improvements of any part or all of a priority funding area.
“Secretary” means the Secretary of Housing and Community Development.
“State fiscal year” means July 1 through June 30.
“Sustainable community” means the part of a priority funding area that:
Has been designated as a sustainable community in accordance with COMAR 05.17.02;
Has been designated as a BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zone under Economic Development Article, Title 5, Subtitle 13, Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Has been designated as a transit-oriented development under Transportation Article, §7-101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
A project shall be submitted for approval by a nonprofit organization.
In order to be eligible for approval under the Program, the project shall satisfy the following requirements:
The project shall provide services to a priority funding area;
The project shall provide services including:
Community services, such as child care, recreational services, and economic development services;
Redevelopment assistance;
Job training for individuals of limited income and related job placement services;
Education;
Crime prevention;
Educator workforce housing; or
Other services approved by the Program; and
The project shall have the written approval of the governing body of each:
County in which the priority funding area benefited by the project is located; and
Municipal corporation in which the priority funding area benefited by the project is located.
Number of Proposals. A nonprofit organization may submit only one project proposal in any State fiscal year.
Forms and Documentation. A project proposal shall be made on standard forms provided by the Program and shall include:
The name and a description of the project to be conducted, and the amount of the tax credit allocation requested;
A description of the problem to be addressed by the project and who will benefit from the project;
A description of the project goals and the measurable objectives;

The priority funding area benefited by the project, together with a statement whether the priority funding area includes, in whole or in part, a sustainable community or a designated neighborhood conservation area;
A description of the experience and capabilities of the nonprofit organization and its key staff members:
In carrying out similar projects; and
In general;
The proposed budget for the project;
A description of the plans for implementing the project;
A copy of the following organizational documentation for the nonprofit organization:
The letter from the Internal Revenue Service granting tax-exempt status under §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code;
Articles of incorporation;
Bylaws; and

A corporate resolution authorizing submission of the application and designating the person or persons authorized to sign documents in connection with the approval of the project, allocation of tax credits, and certification for contributions;
As required by the Program, financial statements, annual operating budget, list of major contributors, and current and anticipated funding sources;
Written approval for the project of the governing body of each:
County in which the priority funding area benefited by the project is located; and
Municipal corporation in which the priority funding area benefited by the project is located; and
Any other information considered necessary by the Program.

Timing. Applications shall be made in accordance with application and competition cycles publicized to nonprofit organizations, local governments, and other interested persons by direct mailing, press release, or other methods selected by the Program.
Threshold Requirements. Each project shall meet the following threshold requirements:
The application shall be complete, providing all of the items and information required in Regulations .04 and .05 of this chapter;
The service or services proposed shall be consistent with the Program purpose and eligible under this chapter and any guidelines issued by the Program;
The application shall identify the priority funding area in which the project will operate; and

If the applicant was awarded an allocation of tax credits for a project during a previous State fiscal year, the applicant shall, in the discretion of the Program, have made substantial progress toward utilizing its previous award of tax credits and satisfying all other Program requirements for the previous project.

Additional Project Review. In approving or disapproving a proposal, and in determining the maximum amount of contributions to an approved project that will be eligible for the Program tax credits, the Department shall consider:
The need for the project in relation to the need for other projects proposed;
The anticipated benefit to the priority funding area and the anticipated effect on the problem to be addressed;
The ability of the applicant to complete the project in a timely and cost-effective manner;
The capacity of the applicant to raise funds for the project, which may include any commitment from a business entity or an individual to make a contribution to the project;
The readiness of the applicant to proceed with the project;
Geographic distribution of projects;
Proposed involvement of local residents or businesses, or both, in the planning or implementation, or both, of the project;
Feasibility of the project, financially, in terms of staffing, and in other respects as determined by the Program; and
Any other relevant factors.
In reviewing applications, the Program may request data and assistance from other units of State government.
Minimum and Maximum Amounts of Tax Credits.
The Program may set guidelines for minimum and maximum amounts of tax credits per project for each round of applications.
The sum of contributions eligible for tax credits for all projects approved for each State fiscal year may not exceed $3,500,000.
Time Period for Using Tax Credits Allocated to a Project.
The Program may establish a deadline for receiving contributions eligible for tax credits.

If, by the Program deadline, the nonprofit organization has not received the maximum amount of contributions for the tax credits allocated to the project, then the remaining tax credits may be used in the discretion of the Secretary:
By extending the deadline for that project; or

For a reserve of tax credits to be allocated by the Secretary to projects approved by the Secretary, all in the Secretary's discretion, with or without review by the evaluation committee described in §F of this regulation.
Selection.
The Secretary shall designate members of the committee to evaluate project applications.
The committee shall evaluate the project proposals based on the guidelines described above and make recommendations to the Secretary for project approval and allocation amounts.
The Secretary shall make all final decisions on project approval and the tax credit allocations.
A decision concerning project approval and tax credit allocation is not a contested case within the meaning of the Administrative Procedure Act or COMAR 05.01.01.02.

The Secretary may delegate to the Assistant Secretary for Neighborhood Revitalization or the Deputy Secretary of the Department the authority to issue the notification letter and execute any agreement required by the Department.

In approving or disapproving a proposal, and in determining the maximum amount of contributions to an approved project that will be eligible for tax credits, the Secretary may give preference to a proposal that benefits a sustainable community or a neighborhood conservation area.
Notification.

Each nonprofit applicant shall receive notice in writing whether or not the project was approved. An approval notice also shall state the maximum amount of contributions to the approved project eligible for the tax credits under the Program.
Notice of approval may be accompanied by an agreement to be entered into by the nonprofit applicant, as required by the Program.
Approval is not effective until the nonprofit applicant has signed and returned the notice and any agreement required by the Program.

If the project is an educator workforce development project, the Department may not approve a project without notifying the County Board of Education, or authorized designee of at least one local school system that benefits from the project.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated and as defined in the Act.
Terms Defined.
“Act” means the Housing and Community Development Article, Title 6, Subtitle 9, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Affordable” means housing costs do not exceed 30 percent of a household's annual income.
“Catalytic revitalization project” means the substantial rehabilitation of a property in the State:
That was formerly owned by the State or the federal government;
In which rehabilitation will foster economic, housing, and community development within the community in which the property is located; and
That is out of service and was formerly used as a college or university, K–12 school, hospital, mental health facility, or military facility or installation.
“Costs” means the costs incurred to develop a catalytic revitalization project and includes the costs of:
Necessary studies, surveys, plans, and specifications;
Architectural, engineering, or other special services, including flood plain studies, environmental audits, and critical area or wetland assessments;
Land and improvements;
Site preparation;
Construction and rehabilitation, as applicable;
Indemnity and surety bonds and premiums on insurance;
Temporary relocation expenses of residents, if applicable; and
Other costs determined to be acceptable by the Department.
“Department” means the Department of Housing and Community Development.
“New construction costs” means the costs associated with the construction of new structures that connect, expand, or integrate the existing structures to be rehabilitated.
“Owned” means a prior ownership interest in real property pursuant to a:
Deed;
Long-term lease;
Federal or State law or legal authority that allowed use and occupation of real property for a governmental purpose; or
Other legal instrument.
“Rehabilitation costs” means the costs associated with the rehabilitation of existing structures.
“Secretary” means the Secretary of Housing and Community Development.
“State tax credit” means the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit allowed under the Act and this chapter.
“Workforce housing” has the meaning stated in Housing and Community Development Article, §4-1801, Annotated Code of Maryland.
An individual, nonprofit organization, or business entity that is proposing a catalytic revitalization project may apply to the Department for an allocation of the available State tax credit.
An applicant shall be in good standing and qualified to do business in Maryland.
n applicant shall have the legal authority to execute an enforceable agreement with the Department.
The Department may accept applications on a first-come, first-served basis or in competitive rounds to be announced by the Department when the State tax credit is available under the Act.
The Department shall consider the following factors when reviewing an application with an emphasis on applications that promote affordable housing and workforce housing:
Historic preservation;
Community development; and
Economic development.
An application submitted to the Department shall:
Be on standard application forms prescribed by the Department;
Be submitted by an eligible applicant under Regulation .03 of this chapter;
Be for a catalytic revitalization project;
Provide a description of how the project will promote the factors listed in §B of this regulation;
Describe if the project will be completed in phases; and
Include any other information required by the Department.

Applications shall be accompanied by all documentation in the form and containing the information specified by the application procedures adopted by the Department, which may vary depending on the type of project.
Application Evaluation.
Each application submitted shall be reviewed by the Department to determine whether all of the information required under this chapter is contained in the application.

Upon submission of all required information, the Department shall undertake an analysis of each application and make a recommendation to the Secretary as to whether a project is eligible for an initial allocation of the State tax credit and any special terms and conditions for a project
The Department shall identify if a project will be in phases and eligible for multiple final tax credit certificates.
Approval of Applications.
If the Department recommends approval of a project for an initial State tax credit allocation, the Department shall present the project to the Secretary.
The Secretary shall approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications an initial State tax credit allocation to be provided according to procedures established by the Secretary.

The Secretary, in the sole discretion of the Secretary, may delegate to an authorized officer of the Department the authority to approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications an initial State tax credit allocation.

The Secretary may require that the applicant execute an enforceable agreement related to the construction and rehabilitation of a catalytic revitalization project and issuance of the State tax credit.

If the Department does not recommend approval of a project for an initial State tax credit allocation, the Department shall issue a written notice of rejection with an evaluation and explanation for rejection.

para.text: In this regulation, “ophthalmological evaluation” means an examination by an ophthalmologist to detect abnormalities of a person's vision and includes, but is not limited to:
Assessment of the cornea, lens, macula, and retina of the eye;
Visual acuity; and
Peripheral vision.

A contestant applying for a license or license renewal shall submit to the Commission an ophthalmological evaluation completed by an ophthalmologist licensed by or eligible for certification by the American Board of Ophthalmology, performed within 90 days before the date of filing the application.
The evaluation under §B shall include an official report of the indirect ophthalmoscopy and slit lamp.
The findings from the evaluation under §§B and C of this regulation shall be reported to the Commission at least 5 business days before the date of the contest.
In order to participate in a contest, a contestant shall pass an ophthalmological evaluation and:
Have visual acuity:
Of at least 20/80 in both eyes, or
Between 20/80 and 20/200, with special permission of the Commission; and
Have 100 percent peripheral vision in both eyes.

In compliance with the blood testing requirements of Business Regulation Article, §4-304.1, Annotated Code of Maryland, a blood sample from an individual desiring to participate in a boxing, kickboxing, or mixed martial arts contest shall be:
Taken by a physician, phlebotomist, or other qualified health care provider chosen by the individual; and
Analyzed by a medical laboratory, certified in accordance with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act, 42 U.S.C. §263(a), for the presence of:
Antibodies to the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and
The antigen of virus hepatitis B.
Only blood tests with negative results shall be submitted to the Commission.
The required negative blood tests:
Shall be submitted to the Commission by an applicant for licensure as a contestant, a contestant, or an authorized representative of the applicant or contestant; and
May not be submitted by the person taking the blood sample, the medical laboratory testing the blood sample, or any other person.
The required negative blood tests shall:
Have been performed within 90 days of the individual's application for a license; and
Except as provided in §E of this regulation, be submitted to the Commission:
At the time the application is submitted to the Commission, or
Not later than the weigh-in for the first contest in which the contestant is to participate following the submittal of the application.

The Commission, in its discretion, may extend the time for the submittal of the required negative blood tests to a time immediately before the contestant's first contest following the issuance of a license.
To constitute documentary evidence satisfactory to the Commission, the negative test results from the medical laboratory shall be:
On the medical laboratory's letterhead; and
Signed by an authorized representative of the medical laboratory.

In addition to submitting the required negative blood tests before a contestant's first contest following the submittal of an application for licensure, a contestant is required to submit the required negative blood tests if:
The contestant previously tested positive for the antibodies to HIV or the antigens of virus hepatitis B; or

The Commission has reasonable cause to believe that the testing of the contestant's blood may not result in a negative test for the presence of the antibodies to HIV or the antigens of virus hepatitis B.

section.heading: Wine and Distilled Spirits Distributorship Appointments.

para.text: Definitions.
In this regulation, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Distilled Spirits.
“Distilled spirits” has the meaning stated in Tax–General Article, §5–101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Distilled spirits” does not include non-conforming beverages as defined in Regulation .20 of this chapter.

“Sole American Source of Supply in Maryland” means a licensed wholesaler that imports a brand of wine or distilled spirits from outside of the United States and that is the sole source of that brand within Maryland under this regulation.
Supplier.
“Supplier” means a licensed manufacturer or permitted nonresident dealer who sells a brand of wine or distilled spirits to a licensed wholesaler for resale to licensed retailers in Maryland.
“Supplier” may include a licensed wholesaler only when they meet the definition of a sole American Source of Supply in Maryland, as designated by the Executive Director.
Wine.
“Wine” has the meaning stated in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1–101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Wine” does not include non-conforming beverages as defined in Regulation .20 of this chapter.
Sole American Source of Supply in Maryland.
A licensed wholesaler may act as a supplier under this regulation only when the licensed wholesaler is the sole American source of supply in Maryland.

A licensed wholesaler who intends to represent a brand of wine or distilled spirits as the sole American source of supply in Maryland under this subsection shall submit a request to the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.
The Executive Director may approve, deny, terminate, or suspend a licensed wholesaler's ability to act as a supplier under this section.

A licensed wholesaler shall notify the Executive Director of a termination of their representation as a sole American source of supply in Maryland as soon as practicable, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A supplier who desires to change the licensed wholesaler it has selected or franchised to distribute a brand of wine or distilled spirits in the State shall provide at least 30 days notice of this intention to the licensed wholesaler and the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A licensed wholesaler who desires to discontinue the sale of a brand of wine or distilled spirits shall provide at least 30 days notice of this intention to the supplier from whom the product was purchased and to the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

If there is evidence that a violation of the law has occurred or that the distribution of a brand or brands of wine or distilled spirits will be adversely affected if the 30-day notice period is followed, the Executive Director may consider any substantial proof that is submitted in writing, and, if circumstances warrant, cause a reduction of this 30-day notice period.

Any brand of wine or distilled spirits affected by the procedure set forth in this regulation which is in the outgoing wholesaler's inventory on or before the conclusion of this notice period shall be purchased and paid for by the supplier or incoming wholesaler at the laid-in cost of the outgoing wholesaler before the incoming wholesaler is allowed to distribute the product in the Maryland market. If a supplier, other than the current brand owner or authorized agent, acquires a brand and wants to designate a wholesaler other than the existing wholesaler, the supplier may not distribute the product until the supplier or incoming wholesaler has purchased the inventory of the outgoing wholesaler at the laid-in cost of the outgoing wholesaler.

A supplier may not select, designate, appoint, or franchise more than one licensed wholesaler to sell or distribute a brand of wine or distilled spirits in Maryland for a period of time any longer than the 30-day notice period mentioned above.
This regulation does not apply to:
A county dispensary acting as a wholesaler; or
Non-conforming beverages as defined under Regulation .20 of this chapter.
Definitions. In this regulation, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
“Geographic territory” means a county in Maryland, as defined in Local Government Article, §1-101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Non-conforming Beverage.
“Non-conforming beverage” means an alcoholic beverage that:
Is intended to be consumed as a single-serving within an individual commercially sealed container with a non-resealable lid or cap;
Contains 20 percent or less alcohol by volume;
Contains in whole or in part wine or distilled spirits; and
Contains a non-alcoholic beverage component.
“Non-conforming beverage” also means a beverage that has been specifically designated by the Executive Director as a non-conforming beverage.
“Non-conforming beverage” does not include:
Beer, as defined in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1-101, Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Any container of alcoholic beverages with multiple servings in a single bottle, can, container, or other package, unless designated by the Executive Director under §C of this regulation.

“Supplier” means a licensed manufacturer, permitted resident dealer, or permitted nonresident dealer who sells a brand of non-conforming beverages to a licensed wholesaler for resale to licensed retailers in Maryland.

Except as authorized under §C of this regulation, non-conforming beverages may be packaged with multiple servings only if each single serving is physically separated into individual serving containers.

A supplier may submit an exemption request from §B of this regulation, for a brand, product, or packaging as a non-conforming beverage to the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A supplier shall notify the Executive Director of selections or appointments of licensed wholesalers for the distribution of a brand of non-conforming beverages in the State, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A supplier who desires to change the licensed wholesaler it has selected or appointed to distribute a brand of non-conforming beverages in the State shall provide at least 30 days’ notice of this intention to the licensed wholesaler and the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A licensed wholesaler who desires to discontinue the sale of a brand of non-conforming beverages shall provide at least 30 days’ notice of this intention to the supplier from whom the product was purchased and to the Executive Director, in a manner prescribed by the Executive Director.

A supplier may not select, designate, or appoint more than one licensed wholesaler to sell or distribute a brand of non-conforming beverages in the same geographic territory for a period of time any longer than the 30-day notice period mentioned above.

It is a violation of §G of this regulation for a supplier to select, designate, appoint, or otherwise permit the distribution of a brand of non-conforming beverage by multiple wholesalers to the same retail location or address.
A supplier who violates §E, G, or H of this regulation may be subject to fine, suspension, or revocation of the license or permit issued by the Executive Director.
A licensed wholesaler may not distribute a brand of non-conforming beverage in a manner that does not conform with this regulation.
A licensed wholesaler who violates §J of this regulation may be subject to fine, suspension, or revocation of the license issued by the Executive Director.
